title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
statement:
You are given an array of strings `tokens` that represents an arithmetic expression in **Reverse Polish Notation** (postfix notation).

Evaluate the expression. Return an integer that represents the value of the expression.

**Note:**
- The valid operators are `+`, `-`, `*`, and `/`.
- Each operand may be an integer or another expression.
- The division between two integers always truncates toward zero.
- There will not be any division by zero.
- The input represents a valid arithmetic expression in a reverse polish notation.
- The answer and all intermediate calculations can be represented in a 32-bit integer.

A stack is the natural fit: push numbers, and whenever you see an operator, pop the two most recent operands, apply the operator, and push the result back.
constraints: tokens[i] is either an operator: '+', '-', '*', or '/', or an integer in the range [-200, 200]

editorial.approach: Iterate through the tokens, pushing numeric operands onto a stack. When an operator token is encountered, pop the top two values from the stack — the second-popped value is the left operand, and the first-popped is the right operand — apply the operator, and push the result back onto the stack. After processing all tokens, the stack contains exactly one value: the final result. Remember that division must truncate toward zero (not floor), which matters for negative results.
